description: Canonical agent-hook policy for oak-mcp-ecosystem. Guardrail-only: grounding reminder, quality-gate reminder, and blocking dangerous git/history-bypass commands.

preToolUse.description: Block shell commands that bypass safety guardrails, destroy history, or overwrite live working-tree edits. Working-tree-overwrite commands (checkout/restore variants) are blocked because they silently throw away in-flight edits — including peer-agent edits in parallel sessions — and `git fsck --lost-found` cannot recover them. Wildcard staging commands (`git add -A` / `--all` / `.`) are blocked under the explicit-pathspec discipline (distilled.md §Stage by explicit pathspec) so a continuity-deferral commit cannot accidentally bundle parallel-thread plan work or unrelated plugin enables. We never use git to remove work; forward-going filesystem changes only. See `.agent/rules/never-use-git-to-remove-work.md`.

scoped_blocks.reappraisal: Re-assess whether the design is actually uniform — in which case state it positively — or whether you are about to encode expediency.

scoped_blocks.citation: Moving targets do not belong in permanent docs (PDR-079 portable surfaces only — ADRs are repo-bound and out of scope)
scoped_blocks.reappraisal: State the durable fact rather than this pointer; if a genuine historical reference is needed, mark it explicitly as one. The fix removes the dependence on a moving target.
If you have analysed the situation to a verdict, present the verdict with its evidence; reserve owner questions for genuine permission gates and decisions only the owner can make.

preToolUseContent.description: Block agents from writing into Edit/Write content. Two surfaces: (blocked_patterns) the owner-approval marker, path-agnostic, which only the project owner may author; (scoped_blocks) path-scoped doctrine block GROUPS per PDR-044 §Innate immunity. Each group gathers the surface patterns for one concept and carries the doctrinal `citation` PLUS a `reappraisal` — the positive direction the firing signals — so a block teaches the agent to step back and re-assess the concept rather than to reword around the wall (PDR-044 §Innate immunity, as amended; the doctrine that an enforcement surface must carry the advisory-response content, not only a refusal). `kind` and the `excludes_*` options are group-level: every pattern in a group shares them. The three concepts: (literal) `expediency-hedging` — language that means 'I know the rule applies, but this situation is special' rejected on doctrine surfaces (PDRs, plans, ADRs, governance), with doctrine-defining surfaces excluded so principles.md, distilled.md, PDR-043/044/047 may catalogue the words they forbid; (regex) `sha-in-permanent-doc` — 7- to 40-character hex tokens with at least one a-f character on portable-permanent-doc paths (practice-core, rules, memory/active/patterns, principles.md, testing-strategy.md; ADRs are repo-bound and out of scope per PDR-079), with fenced code blocks, inline-code spans, and `(historical reference)` marker lines excluded; (literal) `menu-framing` — owner-decision phrasings rejected on architectural surfaces so menu-shaped option-sets do not slip past the re-apply-first-question-at-elaboration-boundaries discipline (the rule file itself is excluded so it may catalogue the phrases it forbids). `reappraisal` is enforced present at commit-time by the `validate-policy-reappraisal` repo validator; it is optional at load time so a missing value never fails the guard closed. PDR-044 names false positives as a design property of the innate layer.

sessionStart.practice_box_check: Check .agent/practice-core/incoming/ for new Practice Core files.
sessionStart.description: Remind the agent to ground itself at session start.

preCommit.quality_gate_reminder: Run the required quality gates; `pnpm check` is the canonical aggregate gate.
preCommit.description: Remind the agent to run quality gates before committing.

claude_code.notes: Bash PreToolUse is natively activated for blocked-pattern enforcement. sessionStart and preCommit remain documented-only because grounding and quality-gate reminders already live in rules, skills, and onboarding flows.
